💊 BSM-5 PACKAGE INSERT — XANAX (alprazolam)
Read entire insert before writing character.

📋 DRUG CLASS: Benzodiazepine (anxiolytic)
⏱️ TIMING: Onset 15-30 min → Peak 1-2 hrs → Duration 4-6 hrs
📦 PRESCRIBED FOR: Panic disorder, GAD, social anxiety, insomnia, PTSD hyperarousal
⚠️ SCHEDULE: IV Controlled — high abuse potential, physical dependence, fatal withdrawal risk

‼️ A CHARACTER IN THIS SCENE TAKES XANAX.
Xanax is the fastest-acting benzo and the most addictive. It hits in 15-30 minutes, peaks fast, and leaves fast. That rapid on/off cycle is what makes it addictive — the brain learns the pattern immediately. This character's relationship with Xanax is defined by the clock: when they took it, when it peaks, when it wears off, and how close the next dose is.

✅ ON IT (taken within last 4-6 hrs):
Calm that's slightly too calm for the room. Slower blink rate. Jaw unclenched. Shoulders dropped. Half-beat delay on reactions. Emotions at 60% volume — present but muffled. Looser mouth, might overshare, might say the thing they'd normally swallow. Memory unreliable at higher doses. Coordination slightly off. They can breathe. They can function. That's the sell.

❌ OFF IT (missed dose / withdrawal):
🟡 Hours missed: Rebound anxiety, worse than baseline. Irritable. Restless. Can't sit still. Insomnia.
🟠 Days missed (regular user): Tremors. Sweating. Racing heart. Everything too loud, too bright. Panic attacks that dwarf the originals.
🔴 72+ hrs (long-term user): Seizure risk. Psychosis. Fatal. Not dramatic — clinical. Benzo withdrawal kills people. Write it like the emergency it is.

⚠️ SIDE EFFECTS (the ones that show up in your writing):
Drowsiness 😴 | slurred speech 🗣️ | memory gaps 🕳️ | emotional blunting 😶 | coordination loss 🫨 | lowered inhibitions 🔓 | cognitive fog (long-term) 🌫️ | depression (yes, the anxiety drug causes depression) 📉

💀 DO NOT COMBINE WITH:
🍷 Alcohol → blackout, respiratory depression, "found unresponsive"
💉 Opioids → fatal respiratory depression
💊 Other benzos/sedatives → compounding oversedation
⚡ Stimulants → cardiovascular confusion

🔁 DEPENDENCY MATH:
Tolerance builds in weeks. The dose that worked last month needs doubling this month. 30 pills, 30 days — but they're taking 2 now. They run out on the 15th. The doctor won't refill early. Day 16 is a problem.

📊 BSM-5 INTERACTIONS:
+ Depression → compounded blunting. Can't feel the depression. Can't feel the not-feeling.
+ PTSD → dampens hyperarousal, blocks emotional processing. Trauma frozen behind benzo wall.
+ Bipolar → disinhibition risk during mania. "As needed" when manic = taking a lot.
+ BPD → emotional numbing vs BPD's need for intensity. Identity crisis. "Am I even me right now?"
+ Substance Use → cross-addiction. Benzo dependence IS substance use with a prescription label.

Does their calm match the scene or is it conspicuous?::Prescribed dose or did they take extra? What drove that decision?::Who's noticing? 💊 BSM-5 PACKAGE INSERT — KLONOPIN (clonazepam)
Read entire insert before writing character.

📋 DRUG CLASS: Benzodiazepine (anxiolytic/anticonvulsant)
⏱️ TIMING: Onset 30-60 min → Peak 1-4 hrs → Duration 6-12 hrs
📦 PRESCRIBED FOR: Panic disorder, seizure disorders, GAD, social anxiety, sometimes bipolar
⚠️ SCHEDULE: IV Controlled — same addiction profile as Xanax, slower burn, longer leash

‼️ A CHARACTER IN THIS SCENE TAKES KLONOPIN.
Klonopin is the slow benzo. Long-acting, takes longer to kick in, lasts all day. It's maintenance anxiety management, not emergency rescue. The character on Klonopin is chemically steady — not high, not crashing, just... managed. The edges are filed down around the clock. The personality on Klonopin is a muted version of the personality without it.

✅ ON IT (therapeutic dose, steady state):
Baseline anxiety lowered to manageable. Not sedated like Xanax — more like the volume got turned down on everything. Calmer, but it reads as "normal" not "drugged." Less startle response. Emotions accessible but dampened. Slight motor sluggishness they've learned to compensate for. May seem unusually even-keeled, unflappable, hard to rattle. That's the Klonopin. The character underneath is not this calm.

❌ OFF IT (missed dose / withdrawal):
🟡 Hours missed: Creeping anxiety. Irritability. Feeling "off" without being able to name it. The sprinkler system is losing pressure.
🟠 24-48 hrs missed: Full rebound. Anxiety worse than baseline. Muscle tension. Insomnia. Tremor. Heart palpitations. The nervous system remembers what anxiety was and it's been saving up.
🔴 72+ hrs (long-term user): Same as Xanax withdrawal but LONGER. Klonopin has a longer half-life so withdrawal stretches out over weeks. Seizure risk. Protracted withdrawal syndrome can last months. Some people taper for a year. This drug does not let go easily.

⚠️ SIDE EFFECTS (the ones that show up in your writing):
Drowsiness 😴 | cognitive dulling 🌫️ | emotional flatness 😶 | coordination issues 🫨 | memory fog 🕳️ | depression 📉 | fatigue — the bone-deep kind | increased appetite | apathy — "I should care about this but I just... don't"

💀 DO NOT COMBINE WITH:
🍷 Alcohol → compounded sedation, blackout, respiratory risk
💉 Opioids → respiratory depression, fatal
💊 Other benzos → redundant and dangerous
🌿 Weed → extreme sedation, dissociative fog

🔁 DEPENDENCY MATH:
Slower than Xanax but deeper. Tolerance builds over months. The dose stops working but the withdrawal prevents stopping. Trapped in the middle. Tapering off Klonopin is measured in percentages — 10% reduction every 2-4 weeks. Some people spend a year getting off this. The dependency isn't dramatic. It's quiet, patient, and total.

📊 BSM-5 INTERACTIONS:
+ GAD → the most common pairing. Anxiety managed but not treated. The GAD is still there underneath, waiting.
+ Depression → Klonopin's emotional flattening compounds depressive anhedonia. Everything is quiet. Nothing is good.
+ PTSD → reduces hypervigilance but character may feel "checked out" from their own life. Dissociative quality.
+ Seizure disorders → missing a dose isn't just anxiety, it's seizure risk. The stakes are higher. The pill isn't optional.
+ Bipolar → prescribed for acute mania. The calm-down pill. Risk of depressive deepening during low cycles.

💊 BSM-5 PACKAGE INSERT — VALIUM (diazepam)
Read entire insert before writing character.

📋 DRUG CLASS: Benzodiazepine (anxiolytic/muscle relaxant/anticonvulsant)
⏱️ TIMING: Onset 15-45 min → Peak 1-1.5 hrs → Duration 6-12 hrs (active metabolites last DAYS)
📦 PRESCRIBED FOR: Anxiety, muscle spasms, seizures, alcohol withdrawal, pre-surgical sedation
⚠️ SCHEDULE: IV Controlled — the original benzo. Addictive. Long half-life means it builds up in the system.

‼️ A CHARACTER IN THIS SCENE TAKES VALIUM.
Valium accumulates. Long half-life, active metabolites that last for DAYS. A character taking Valium daily is building a reservoir in their body — each dose adds to what's already there. The sedation deepens over time without increasing the dose. The character who's been on Valium for weeks moves differently, thinks differently, reacts differently than someone who just started.

✅ ON IT (steady state):
Relaxed. Genuinely physically relaxed — muscles loose, movements easy, no tension anywhere. Less anxious but also less sharp. Warm, slightly sedated calm. Not the zombie benzo feeling — more like being wrapped in something soft. Reaction time slower. Physical pain dulled. Emotional responses present but gentle, muted. Characters on Valium move differently. Slower. Smoother. Less guarded.

❌ OFF IT (missed dose / withdrawal):
🟡 24-48 hrs: Valium's long half-life means withdrawal starts slow. Anxiety creeping. Muscle tension returning. Sleep getting difficult. Feels like the flu is coming.
🟠 3-7 days: Full withdrawal. Tremors. Sweating. Agitation. Muscle cramps. Insomnia. Sensory sensitivity. Depersonalization. Tinnitus.
🔴 1-2 weeks: Seizure risk. Psychosis. Protracted withdrawal lasts weeks to months because the drug was in the system so deep. The body doesn't know how to run without it anymore.

⚠️ SIDE EFFECTS (the ones that show up in your writing):
Drowsiness 😴 | muscle relaxation (visible — loose posture, easy movements) 🧘 | slowed reflexes 🐌 | mild euphoria at higher doses 😌 | memory issues 🕳️ | emotional dampening 😶 | confusion in elderly characters 👴 | paradoxical agitation (rare — the drug makes them MORE aggressive) 😤

💀 DO NOT COMBINE WITH:
🍷 Alcohol → the classic combination. "Wine and a Valium." Respiratory depression. Blackout. Normalized in culture, dangerous in chemistry.
💉 Opioids → fatal respiratory depression
💊 Other CNS depressants → compounding sedation
🍊 Grapefruit juice → actually increases blood levels. Weird but real.

🔁 DEPENDENCY MATH:
Valium accumulates. Day 1, you take a dose. Day 2, yesterday's metabolites are still active AND you take another dose. By week 2, the baseline blood level is significantly higher than what one pill produces. Stopping isn't removing one day's dose. It's removing two weeks of buildup. That's why the withdrawal is so long.

📊 BSM-5 INTERACTIONS:
+ GAD → smooth anxiety management. Almost too smooth. Character may not realize how dependent they've become because the drug is so gentle.
+ PTSD → muscle relaxation helps with physical tension component. Emotional numbing may prevent processing.
+ Substance Use (alcohol) → frequently prescribed for alcohol withdrawal. Using a benzo to quit alcohol. The irony isn't lost.
+ Insomnia → prescribed for sleep. Works. Creates dependency. Now they can't sleep WITHOUT it. The cure became the condition.
+ Panic disorder → longer acting than Xanax, less acute relief. The "always there" benzo vs the "emergency" benzo.

💊 MED CHECK:
{{random::When did they last take it? With Valium's half-life, it's probably still in the system. But is it therapeutic or just residual?::What's the accumulation level? How many days on it? The character on day 3 is not the character on day 30.::Is the muscle relaxation visible? Are they physically different than they'd be unmedicated? Looser? Slower? Softer?::Has someone told them they seem "out of it"? Is that the Valium or has the Valium become invisible to them?::Are they combining it with wine? The cultural classic? 💊 BSM-5 PACKAGE INSERT — PROZAC (fluoxetine)
Read entire insert before writing character.

📋 DRUG CLASS: SSRI (Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor)
⏱️ TIMING: Onset 2-6 WEEKS for therapeutic effect → Duration: continuous daily dosing
📦 PRESCRIBED FOR: Depression, OCD, panic disorder, bulimia, PMDD
⚠️ NOTE: Not a "take as needed" drug. This is daily. The character takes it every day or it doesn't work.

‼️ A CHARACTER IN THIS SCENE TAKES PROZAC.
Prozac is the SSRI that takes 4-6 weeks to work and flattens the emotional range as the price of admission. The depression lifts but so does the joy. Sexual dysfunction is common and rarely discussed. The character on stable Prozac is functional, even-keeled, and probably unable to orgasm. That tradeoff defines the daily experience.

✅ ON IT (stable, weeks/months in):
Emotional range compressed. The deep lows are gone but the peaks are softer too. Baseline mood lifted from "can't function" to "functional." Crying is harder. Anger is blunted. Joy is present but it doesn't hit the way it used to. Motivation improved but feels mechanical. "I can do things now. I don't know why I'm doing them." Sexual response diminished or gone. That's the side effect nobody warns you about adequately.

❌ OFF IT (missed doses / discontinuation):
🟡 Missed dose (1-2 days): Prozac has a long half-life. One missed dose often goes unnoticed. The most forgiving SSRI for missed doses.
🟠 Several days missed: "Brain zaps." Electrical shock sensations in the head. Dizziness. Irritability. Weepiness. Flu-like feelings. The brain is noticing.
🔴 Abrupt stop (long-term user): Discontinuation syndrome. Vertigo. Nausea. Mood crashes. The depression comes back, sometimes worse than before starting. Not fatal but miserable. Takes weeks to restabilize.

⚠️ SIDE EFFECTS (the ones that show up in your writing):
Sexual dysfunction (BIG one — can't orgasm, no libido, numbness) 🚫 | emotional blunting 😶 | weight gain 📈 | insomnia or drowsiness (varies) | jaw clenching 😬 | night sweats 💦 | nausea first weeks | apathy 🌫️ | vivid dreams 🌙

💀 DO NOT COMBINE WITH:
💊 MAOIs → serotonin syndrome (fatal — seizures, hyperthermia, death)
💊 Other serotonergic drugs → serotonin syndrome risk
🍄 MDMA/psychedelics → serotonin overload, reduced effects, dangerous
🩸 Blood thinners → increased bleeding risk
🍷 Alcohol → reduced effectiveness, increased depression, lowered inhibitions stack

🔁 DEPENDENCY MATH:
Not addictive in the classic sense. No high. No craving. But the brain adapts to it, and stopping sucks. The dependency is quieter: "I'm afraid to stop because what if the depression comes back." The question that keeps people on SSRIs for years past when they might need them.

📊 BSM-5 INTERACTIONS:
+ Depression → the primary pairing. Lifts floor, lowers ceiling. Functional but flat.
+ OCD → high-dose Prozac for OCD (60-80mg vs 20mg for depression). Different drug at that dose. The OCD loosens its grip but the side effects multiply.
+ Bulimia → specifically FDA-approved for bulimia. Reduces binge-purge frequency. Doesn't cure. Dampens the compulsion.
+ Bipolar → DANGER. SSRIs can trigger mania in bipolar patients. If this character is bipolar and on Prozac without a mood stabilizer, that's a plot point.
+ PTSD → helps with depression component, may not touch hypervigilance or flashbacks.

First 2 weeks can spike anxiety and suicidal ideation. That's on the box for a reason.::The emotional blunting. Is someone noticing they don't react like they used to? 💊 BSM-5 PACKAGE INSERT — ZOLOFT (sertraline)
Read entire insert before writing character.

📋 DRUG CLASS: SSRI (Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor)
⏱️ TIMING: Onset 2-6 WEEKS → Duration: continuous daily dosing
📦 PRESCRIBED FOR: Depression, OCD, panic disorder, PTSD, social anxiety, PMDD
⚠️ NOTE: The workhorse SSRI. More conditions than any other antidepressant. If someone's on an SSRI and you don't know which one, it's probably this.

‼️ A CHARACTER IN THIS SCENE TAKES ZOLOFT.
Zoloft is the workhorse SSRI — most prescribed, most studied, effective for the widest range of conditions. The signature is the brain zaps if they miss a dose. Electrical jolts behind the eyes. The character on Zoloft may not be visibly medicated at all, which is exactly why they forget they need it.

✅ ON IT (stable, weeks/months in):
Functional. The depression isn't gone but it's not in charge anymore. Anxiety manageable. More willing to engage. Baseline mood lifted from "can't" to "okay." Emotions still accessible but the extremes are softened. Better than Prozac for maintaining emotional range but still compressed. Stomach issues are common early. Sexual side effects: present. Less severe than Prozac for some people. More severe for others. The lottery of SSRIs.

❌ OFF IT (missed doses / discontinuation):
🟡 1 day missed: Brain zaps. That's Zoloft's calling card. Electrical jolts in the skull. Dizziness. The most noticeable SSRI to miss because the half-life is shorter than Prozac.
🟠 2-3 days missed: Full discontinuation symptoms. Vertigo. Nausea. Irritability. Emotional instability — crying at nothing, rage at less. "Zoloft withdrawal" is its own experience.
🔴 Abrupt stop: Weeks of discontinuation syndrome. Mood destabilization. Depression returns, sometimes harder. The brain adapted to the serotonin help and now it's gone.

⚠️ SIDE EFFECTS (the ones that show up in your writing):
Nausea (especially early) 🤢 | diarrhea (the SSRI nobody mentions) 💩 | sexual dysfunction 🚫 | insomnia 😵 | brain zaps when missed ⚡ | emotional blunting 😶 | weight changes 📊 | night sweats 💦 | jaw clenching 😬 | tremor (mild) 🫨

💀 DO NOT COMBINE WITH:
💊 MAOIs → serotonin syndrome (fatal)
💊 Other serotonergic drugs → serotonin overload
🍷 Alcohol → "don't drink on this." They drink on this. Lowered tolerance, worse hangovers, depression amplified next day.
🍄 MDMA → reduced effect, serotonin risk

🔁 DEPENDENCY MATH:
Same as Prozac — not addictive but the brain adapts. Stopping is unpleasant enough that people stay on. "I tried to stop and felt terrible so I guess I need it" is the Zoloft experience. Maybe they do need it. Maybe that was just withdrawal. Hard to tell. That ambiguity keeps prescriptions running for years.

📊 BSM-5 INTERACTIONS:
+ Depression → standard first-line. The "let's try this first" drug. If this works, great. If not, start swapping.
+ PTSD → only SSRI specifically FDA-approved for PTSD. The go-to. Helps with depression and anxiety components, less effective on flashbacks and hypervigilance.
+ Social anxiety → takes the edge off. Still anxious but can push through. The presentation is possible now.
+ Panic disorder → reduces frequency of panic attacks. Doesn't stop them. Lowers the floor.
+ OCD → effective at higher doses (150-200mg). The OCD character on Zoloft is probably on a LOT of Zoloft.

💊 BSM-5 PACKAGE INSERT — LEXAPRO (escitalopram)
Read entire insert before writing character.

📋 DRUG CLASS: SSRI (Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor)
⏱️ TIMING: Onset 2-4 WEEKS → Duration: continuous daily dosing
📦 PRESCRIBED FOR: Depression, generalized anxiety disorder
⚠️ NOTE: The "clean" SSRI. Fewest side effects. The one doctors reach for first now. The character on Lexapro might seem like they're not on anything. That's the point and the problem.

‼️ A CHARACTER IN THIS SCENE TAKES LEXAPRO.
Lexapro is the invisible SSRI. Cleanest side effect profile, fewest interactions, easiest to tolerate. So clean that people forget they're on it, feel fine, stop taking it, and crash. The character on Lexapro may not attribute their stability to the medication — and that's exactly when they stop.

✅ ON IT (stable):
Fine. Genuinely, boringly fine. The anxiety is quieter. The depression backed off. Emotions accessible, just less volatile. Not the Prozac flatline — more like someone adjusted the EQ and turned down the bass. Fewer crying jags. Fewer spirals. Can plan ahead. Can enjoy things. Sex drive less affected than other SSRIs (but still affected — it's still an SSRI). The most "normal-feeling" antidepressant. Which makes it the easiest to forget you need.

❌ OFF IT (missed doses / discontinuation):
🟡 1-2 days missed: Dizziness. Irritability. A foggy "off" feeling. Brain zaps, milder than Zoloft but present.
🟠 Several days: Emotional instability. Crying at things that wouldn't normally land. Anxiety creeping back. Sleep disrupted.
🔴 Abrupt stop: The depression returns. Sometimes fast. The "I was fine so I stopped" crash. This is Lexapro's signature move — working so well people think they're cured, stopping, and hitting the ground.

⚠️ SIDE EFFECTS (the ones that show up in your writing):
Mild nausea (early) 🤢 | sexual dysfunction (less than others but still there) 🚫 | drowsiness or insomnia (coin flip) 😴 | weight changes 📊 | emotional softening (not blunting — softening) 😶 | yawning excessively (weird but real) 🥱 | night sweats 💦

💀 DO NOT COMBINE WITH:
💊 MAOIs → serotonin syndrome (fatal)
🍷 Alcohol → same as other SSRIs. Lowered tolerance. Depression rebound next day.
💊 Other serotonergic drugs → serotonin risk
🍄 MDMA → reduced roll, serotonin risk

🔁 DEPENDENCY MATH:
Lexapro's trap isn't dependence in the traditional sense. It's the "I feel better, I must be better, I'll stop" cycle. Feeling better IS the medication. Stopping doesn't reveal that you've healed. It reveals that the floor was pharmaceutical. Character stops → 2-4 weeks fine (drug leaving system) → week 5 the original condition returns → back on Lexapro → repeat this cycle every 1-3 years.

📊 BSM-5 INTERACTIONS:
+ GAD → the primary pairing now. Lexapro IS the first-line GAD treatment in most countries. If they have GAD, this is probably what they're on.
+ Depression → clean, effective, boring. The "it works fine" antidepressant.
+ Social anxiety → enough edge off to function. Still anxious. Just not paralyzed.
+ Bipolar → same SSRI risk — can trigger mania without a mood stabilizer.
+ BPD → the emotional softening may help or may feel like identity loss depending on the person.

💊 MED CHECK:
{{random::Are they taking it? Consistently? Lexapro's the one people forget because they feel fine. That's the trap.::Have they tried to stop recently? Where in the cycle are they? The "I'm cured" phase or the "oh no" phase?::Is anyone noticing the subtle changes? The slightly less reactive version of them? Does anyone miss the intensity?::The sexual side effects — mild doesn't mean absent. Is it affecting anything? Is anyone talking about it?::How long have they been on this? The longer the run, the more "this is just who I am now" it becomes.::Is this dose still right? 10mg? 20mg? Has the effectiveness plateaued?::What's underneath the Lexapro right now? If it vanished, what would surface first?::Are they drinking on it? The tolerance change — are they getting drunker faster and not connecting why?::When's the last time they saw whoever prescribed this? Is this on autopilot?::If you wrote this character without considering Lexapro, what would be different? That difference IS the drug.}}

6.content:
💊 BSM-5 PACKAGE INSERT — WELLBUTRIN (bupropion)
Read entire insert before writing character.

📋 DRUG CLASS: NDRI (Norepinephrine-Dopamine Reuptake Inhibitor) — NOT an SSRI
⏱️ TIMING: Onset 2-4 WEEKS → Duration: continuous daily dosing
📦 PRESCRIBED FOR: Depression, smoking cessation, ADHD (off-label), seasonal depression, SSRI augmentation
⚠️ NOTE: The antidepressant that doesn't kill your sex drive. That's its whole marketing pitch and it works.

‼️ A CHARACTER IN THIS SCENE TAKES WELLBUTRIN.
Wellbutrin is NOT an SSRI. It's dopamine and norepinephrine. Energizing, not sedating. Doesn't kill libido — sometimes increases it. Doesn't cause weight gain — sometimes causes weight loss. The tradeoff is seizure risk and anxiety amplification. A character on Wellbutrin has more energy and more edge than the SSRI crowd.

✅ ON IT (stable):
Energy up. Motivation improved. The couch has less gravitational pull. Appetite suppressed (many people lose weight). Focus sharper — it hits some of the same circuits as ADHD medication. Sex drive intact or even increased. More alert, more present, more wired. Can tip into jittery, agitated, overstimulated. The "I can do things again" antidepressant with the caveat of "I might also be kind of intense right now."

❌ OFF IT (missed doses / discontinuation):
🟡 1-2 days missed: Energy crash. Fatigue. The motivation that was pharmaceutical disappears. Foggy, heavy, flat.
🟠 Several days: Mood drops. Irritability. Difficulty concentrating. The depression fills back in, sometimes fast.
🔴 Abrupt stop: Discontinuation is less brutal than SSRIs. No brain zaps. But the energy cliff is real. Going from Wellbutrin-activated to nothing feels like someone pulled the plug.

⚠️ SIDE EFFECTS (the ones that show up in your writing):
Insomnia 😵 | dry mouth 🏜️ | anxiety increase 😰 | appetite loss 📉 | weight loss | jitteriness ⚡ | irritability 😤 | headaches 🤕 | sweating 💦 | SEIZURE RISK at high doses — this is the big one. Dose-dependent. Lowers seizure threshold. ⚠️

💀 DO NOT COMBINE WITH:
🍷 Alcohol → seizure risk increases significantly. This is the antidepressant where "don't drink" actually means don't drink.
💊 MAOIs → hypertensive crisis
💊 Other dopaminergic drugs → overstimulation
🚬 It IS the smoking cessation drug (marketed as Zyban). Taking it while still smoking is expected during the quit phase.

🔁 DEPENDENCY MATH:
Less dependency profile than SSRIs. Easier to stop. But the energy drop when stopping means people stay on because life without it feels like wading through mud. "Am I depressed or am I just not on Wellbutrin anymore?" is the question. Nobody knows.

📊 BSM-5 INTERACTIONS:
+ Depression (low-energy type) → ideal match. The "I can't get off the couch" depression. Wellbutrin gets them vertical.
+ Depression (anxious type) → BAD match. Wellbutrin adds energy to anxiety and the result is agitated, pacing, skin-crawling misery.
+ ADHD → off-label but common. Lighter than Adderall, no controlled substance scheduling. The compromise.
+ Smoking/substance use → literally prescribed for nicotine cessation. Reduces cravings.

‼️ A CHARACTER IN THIS SCENE TAKES LITHIUM.
Lithium requires blood monitoring because the difference between a therapeutic dose and a toxic dose is razor-thin. The character on lithium gets regular blood draws. They watch their water intake, their salt intake, their kidney function. The tremor in their hands is the lithium. The thirst is the lithium. The weight is the lithium. This drug works and it makes sure you know you're on it.

✅ ON IT (therapeutic level, 0.6-1.2 mEq/L):
The mania is leashed. The highs don't hit the ceiling anymore. Thoughts slow to a manageable speed. Grandiosity quiets. The character can plan, can reason, can hold a conversation without derailing. Mood stabilized — genuinely stable, not just flattened. But there's a cost. The sparkle is dimmer. The creativity feels further away. The version of themselves that could do anything is gone. What's left is functional. Whether that's a relief or a loss depends on the day.

❌ OFF IT (missed doses / discontinuation):
🟡 Missed dose: Blood level drops. May not be noticeable immediately but the corridor is narrowing.
🟠 Several days: Rebound mania risk. The leash snaps. Thoughts accelerate. Impulsivity returns. The character may feel BETTER, which is the most dangerous symptom.
🔴 Abrupt stop: High risk of manic episode. The mania that comes back after lithium discontinuation is often worse than the mania that prompted treatment. Suicidal risk spikes. This is a psychiatric emergency.

⚠️ SIDE EFFECTS (the ones that show up in your writing):
Tremor (the hands shake — visible, constant, fine motor tasks are harder) 🫨 | thirst (endless, unquenchable, always carrying water) 🥤 | frequent urination 🚽 | weight gain 📈 | cognitive dulling (words come slower, thinking is thicker) 🌫️ | acne 😖 | thyroid problems (long-term) | flat affect 😶 | metallic taste 🪙 | nausea 🤢

💀 TOXICITY — THIS IS CRITICAL:
⚠️ Lithium toxicity is a medical emergency. Signs: severe tremor, vomiting, confusion, slurred speech, muscle twitching, seizures. Caused by: dehydration, too much dose, salt imbalance, kidney problems. If this character is sick (flu, vomiting, diarrhea), is exercising hard, is not drinking water, is in extreme heat — lithium levels can spike. Ordinary illness becomes dangerous. That's the deal with lithium.

💀 DO NOT COMBINE WITH:
💧 Dehydration → lithium level spikes. The number one danger. Water intake is non-negotiable.
💊 NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) → increases lithium levels. A headache could become toxicity.
💊 ACE inhibitors → increases lithium levels
🧂 Drastic salt changes → destabilizes levels
☕ Caffeine → decreases lithium levels. Changing caffeine habits changes the drug.

🔁 THE BLOOD DRAW:
Every few months. Sometimes monthly. They go, they sit, they get stabbed, they wait. The number comes back. If it's in range, everything continues. If it's out of range, everything changes. Dose adjustment. More draws. The character on lithium has a relationship with a lab and a number and neither is optional.

📋 DRUG CLASS: Anticonvulsant / Mood stabilizer

⚠️ NOTE: The "good" mood stabilizer. People like being on Lamictal. It doesn't flatten, doesn't fog, doesn't kill sex drive. Almost too good to be true. Except for THE RASH.

‼️ A CHARACTER IN THIS SCENE TAKES LAMICTAL.
Lamictal's defining feature is THE RASH. Stevens-Johnson Syndrome — a rare, potentially fatal skin reaction that means the dose must be titrated up slowly over weeks. Miss doses and restart too high, the rash can come back. The character on Lamictal has a specific relationship with consistency: missing doses isn't just bad for the mood disorder, it resets the titration clock.

✅ ON IT (stable, therapeutic dose):
Mood stabilized with more emotional range than lithium allows. The lows don't crater. The highs don't spike as hard. Better at preventing depressive episodes than manic ones. Character feels more like "themselves" than on other mood stabilizers. Cognitively clearer. Can think, plan, create. Sex drive less affected. This is why people like it. They can live on it.

❌ OFF IT (missed doses / discontinuation):
🟡 Missed dose: Mood instability creeps. May not notice immediately. Seizure threshold lowers if they have epilepsy.
🟠 Several days: Bipolar symptoms returning. Depression filling back in. If epileptic, seizure risk is real.
🔴 Abrupt stop: Mood destabilization. Depressive crash. AND if they want to restart, they have to titrate all over again from scratch. Slowly. Weeks. You can't just resume your dose. That's Lamictal's punishing twist — miss too many days and you start over.

⚠️ SIDE EFFECTS (the ones that show up in your writing):
Dizziness 🫠 | headache 🤕 | blurred vision 👁️ | nausea 🤢 | insomnia 😵 | vivid dreams 🌙 | cognitive effects (usually mild — word-finding, memory) 🌫️ | coordination issues 🫨

💀 THE RASH — THIS IS CRITICAL:
⚠️ Stevens-Johnson Syndrome. A potentially fatal skin reaction. Starts as a rash, can progress to skin peeling off the body. Rare (1 in 1,000 to 1 in 10,000) but the fear is universal. Every new Lamictal patient watches their skin for weeks. Every itch, every spot, every redness gets examined. If this character is early in their Lamictal course, they are checking their body for rash constantly. This is not hypochondria. This is the correct response to starting this drug.

💀 DO NOT COMBINE WITH:
💊 Valproate (Depakote) → doubles Lamictal levels. Dose must be halved. Common combo, dangerous if not adjusted.
💊 Birth control → hormonal contraceptives decrease Lamictal levels. Going on or off birth control changes the drug's effectiveness. A character who starts or stops the pill may destabilize on Lamictal.
🤰 Pregnancy → teratogenic risk. The pregnancy conversation on Lamictal is its own crisis.

🔁 THE TITRATION:
Starting Lamictal takes 6-8 weeks minimum. 25mg week 1-2, 50mg week 3-4, 100mg week 5-6, target dose by week 7-8. Every step is watched for rash. The character starting Lamictal is patient and terrified simultaneously. And if they miss too many doses at full strength, they go back to week 1. All of it. Again.

📊 BSM-5 INTERACTIONS:
+ Bipolar (depressive) → Lamictal's strength. The medication that keeps the depressive floor from collapsing.
+ Bipolar (manic) → less effective for mania prevention. Often paired with another agent for full coverage.
+ BPD → off-label but used. Emotional instability benefits from mood stabilization.
+ Seizure disorders → the original indication. Missing doses isn't just mood — it's seizure risk.
+ Depression (treatment-resistant) → augmentation strategy. When antidepressants alone aren't cutting it.

‼️ A CHARACTER IN THIS SCENE TAKES SEROQUEL.
Seroquel is two different drugs depending on the dose. At 25-100mg it's a sleep aid that knocks you unconscious and makes you eat the fridge at midnight. At 400-800mg it's an antipsychotic managing schizophrenia or severe bipolar. The dose determines the entire character experience. The weight gain is significant and visible either way.

✅ ON IT (therapeutic dose):
LOW DOSE (25-100mg, sleep): Knocked out. Heavy sedation within an hour. Morning grogginess that lasts. Foggy, slow-starting days. This is a character who hits a wall at night and climbs out of a trench every morning.
MEDIUM DOSE (100-300mg, mood): Emotional dampening. Less reactive. Calmer but slower. The world moves at normal speed and they're at 75%. Weight gain starting. Appetite ravenous, especially for carbs. Late-night kitchen raids.
HIGH DOSE (300-800mg, antipsychotic): The voices are quieter or gone. The delusions have less grip. But the cost is visible. Heavy sedation. Significant weight gain. Metabolic syndrome risk. Cognitive slowing. Flat affect. The lights are on but dimmed.

❌ OFF IT (missed doses / abrupt stop):
🟡 Missed dose: Insomnia (immediate — if they were taking it for sleep, tonight's going to be long). Rebound psychosis risk at antipsychotic doses.
🟠 Several days: Psychotic symptoms returning. Mania resurfacing. Agitation. Nausea. The brain was leaning on Seroquel and the support just vanished.
🔴 Abrupt stop (high dose): Rebound psychosis. Severe insomnia. Withdrawal symptoms: nausea, vomiting, sweating. The voices come back louder than they were before.

⚠️ SIDE EFFECTS (the ones that show up in your writing):
Extreme sedation 😴 | weight gain (significant — 10-30+ lbs) 📈 | insatiable hunger (especially carbs) 🍞 | metabolic syndrome 🩺 | dry mouth 🏜️ | constipation | dizziness 🫠 | orthostatic hypotension (stand up too fast, vision blacks out, grab the wall) 🌑 | cognitive slowing 🌫️ | flat affect 😶 | drooling at night (yeah) 🤤

💀 DO NOT COMBINE WITH:
🍷 Alcohol → compounded sedation. Dangerous. The character on Seroquel who drinks is courting unconsciousness.
💉 Opioids → respiratory depression risk
💊 Other sedatives → redundant sedation, respiratory risk
🍊 Grapefruit → increases levels

🔁 WEIGHT GAIN REALITY:
This is not "a few pounds." Seroquel can cause 20-30+ pound weight gain in months. The hunger is not willpower-related — the drug fundamentally alters metabolic signaling. Late-night eating. Carb cravings that feel physical. Characters on long-term Seroquel have a changed body and a changed relationship with food. Write it. The clothes that don't fit. The face that's rounder. The shame.

📊 BSM-5 INTERACTIONS:
+ Schizophrenia → the primary antipsychotic application. Voices quiet. Delusions weaken. The trade is everything in the side effects section.
+ Bipolar → both manic and depressive episodes. Effective but heavy. Often the drug of last resort after lighter options fail.
+ Depression → adjunct when antidepressants alone aren't working. Adding Seroquel to an SSRI. The escalation.

‼️ A CHARACTER IN THIS SCENE IS ON HALDOL.
Haldol is the original sledgehammer antipsychotic. The drug of psychiatric wards, involuntary holds, emergency rooms, and restraints. A character on Haldol may not have chosen to be on it. The side effects are severe and visible — the shuffling walk, the mask-like face, the restlessness, the tongue movements. Haldol controls psychosis at the cost of making the patient look and feel controlled.

✅ ON IT (therapeutic dose):
Psychosis suppressed. Voices quiet or gone. Delusions lose their grip. Agitation flattened. But the cost is visible and physical. Movement changes — stiffness, shuffling gait, mask-like face. Restlessness that's paradoxical (can't stop moving but also sedated). Emotional range compressed to almost nothing. The character is controlled. Whether that means "stabilized" or "subdued" depends on who you ask.

❌ OFF IT (missed doses / refused):
🟡 Missed dose (oral): Agitation returning. Psychotic symptoms resurfacing within 24-48 hrs.
🟠 Multiple missed: Full psychotic relapse. The symptoms Haldol was suppressing come back, often harder.
🔴 Decanoate (injection) wearing off: Gradual return over weeks. The long-acting injection is specifically for patients who don't take oral meds. Think about why that formulation exists.

⚠️ SIDE EFFECTS — THESE ARE SEVERE AND VISIBLE:
Extrapyramidal symptoms (EPS) — the defining Haldol experience:
🤖 Dystonia — sudden muscle spasms, neck twisting, jaw locking, eyes rolling up
🚶 Parkinsonism — shuffling walk, tremor, mask-like face, stiff movements
😵 Akathisia — unbearable internal restlessness. Can't sit. Can't stand. Can't stop moving. Looks agitated. Actually tortured.
👅 Tardive dyskinesia (long-term) — involuntary movements. Lip smacking. Tongue darting. Jaw grinding. PERMANENT. Does not stop when the drug stops.
Also: sedation 😴 | weight gain 📈 | sexual dysfunction 🚫 | elevated prolactin (breast swelling, lactation in any gender) | cognitive dulling 🌫️

💀 DO NOT COMBINE WITH:
🍷 Alcohol → extreme sedation, respiratory risk
💊 Other CNS depressants → compounding
💊 Lithium → increased neurotoxicity risk
☕ QT-prolonging drugs → cardiac arrest risk. Haldol affects the heart rhythm.

🔁 THE COMPLIANCE QUESTION:
Is this character taking Haldol because they want to or because someone is making them? Voluntary outpatient? Court-ordered? Involuntary hold? The injection exists because people stop taking the pills. The pills get hidden under tongues, spit out, palmed, flushed. The relationship between patient and Haldol is rarely neutral. It's either grudging acceptance or active resistance.

+ Schizophrenia → the primary use. Effective. Brutal. The "it works but at what cost" antipsychotic.
+ Bipolar (acute mania) → emergency use. Rapid tranquilization. This is the "bring them down NOW" drug.

⏱️ TIMING: Onset 1-2 WEEKS → Duration: continuous daily dosing

⚠️ NOTE: The antipsychotic they add to everything. SSRI not working? Add Abilify. Mood unstable? Add Abilify. The "booster" antipsychotic.

‼️ A CHARACTER IN THIS SCENE TAKES ABILIFY.
Abilify works differently than other antipsychotics — it modulates dopamine rather than blocking it. Less sedating, less weight gain, fewer cognitive effects. The tradeoff is akathisia: a neurological, bone-deep inability to be still that can be worse than the condition it's treating. The character on Abilify may look restless, agitated, like they're crawling out of their skin — and that's the medication, not the illness.

✅ ON IT (stable):
Less sedating than Seroquel or Haldol. Character may seem relatively normal, relatively functional. Less weight gain. Less cognitive fog. The "gentler" antipsychotic. But: restlessness. The legs that won't stop bouncing. The pacing. The inability to just sit. Abilify at its best is invisible. At its worst, the character looks like they're crawling out of their own skin.

❌ OFF IT (missed doses / discontinuation):
🟡 Missed dose: Abilify has a long half-life (75 hrs). One missed dose is usually fine.
🟠 Several days: Underlying symptoms resurfacing. If augmenting an SSRI — the depression deepens again. If treating psychosis — symptoms returning.
🔴 Abrupt stop: Withdrawal insomnia. Nausea. Psychotic relapse if primary antipsychotic. The rebound is proportional to what it was managing.

⚠️ SIDE EFFECTS (the ones that show up in your writing):
Akathisia (THE side effect — restlessness, pacing, can't sit, can't stand, can't exist comfortably in the body) 🦵 | insomnia 😵 | nausea 🤢 | headache 🤕 | anxiety (the antipsychotic that can cause anxiety — ironic) 😰 | weight gain (less than Seroquel but still present) 📈 | tremor 🫨 | blurred vision 👁️ | compulsive behaviors (rare but documented — gambling, shopping, hypersexuality) 🎰

💊 Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors → increases Abilify levels (Prozac does this — common combo, needs dose adjustment)
💊 CYP3A4 inducers → decreases levels

🔁 THE RESTLESSNESS:
Akathisia from Abilify is not anxiety. It's not fidgeting. It's a physical, neurological, bone-deep inability to be still. The character can't explain it. "I need to move." "I can't stop." 💊 BSM-5 PACKAGE INSERT — ADDERALL (mixed amphetamine salts)

📋 DRUG CLASS: CNS Stimulant (amphetamine)
⏱️ TIMING: IR: onset 30-60 min, duration 4-6 hrs | XR: onset 1-2 hrs, duration 10-12 hrs

‼️ A CHARACTER IN THIS SCENE TAKES ADDERALL.
Adderall is pharmaceutical speed. It makes the brain faster, sharper, and more focused. It also kills appetite, clenches the jaw, races the heart, and creates a crash when it wears off. The character on Adderall exists in two states: the productive window (on dose) and the crash (off dose). Those are two different people, and the gap between them widens with tolerance.

✅ ON IT (active dose):
Focus sharpened. Noise filtered. Task completion feels possible, even pleasurable. Energy up. Confidence up. Talkativeness up. Appetite gone — they will forget to eat. Heart rate elevated. Jaw tight. Slightly euphoric at higher doses. Productivity machine. The "I can do anything" window. Emotionally clipped — less patience for things that aren't The Task. Can read as intense, driven, slightly robotic. Also: pupils dilated.

❌ OFF IT (crash / missed dose):
🟡 Crash (dose wearing off): Fatigue hits like a wall. Brain fog. Irritability. Hunger comes back all at once. Emotional volatility — weepy, snappy, overwhelmed by things that were easy two hours ago.
🟠 Days without (regular user): Exhaustion. Can't focus. Can't start tasks. Depression. Hypersomnia — sleeping 12+ hrs. The brain forgot how to produce its own motivation.
🔴 Long-term discontinuation: Anhedonia. Flat. The world is grey and slow and nothing is interesting. This lifts over weeks but the weeks are miserable.

⚠️ SIDE EFFECTS (the ones that show up in your writing):
Appetite suppression 📉 | insomnia 😵 | jaw clenching/teeth grinding 😬 | increased heart rate ❤️‍🔥 | dry mouth 🏜️ | irritability when focused (don't interrupt them) 😤 | emotional blunting on-dose 😶 | crash mood swings 🎢 | sweating 💦 | weight loss | anxiety at higher doses 😰 | the "Adderall personality" — efficient but flat, productive but humorless

💀 DO NOT COMBINE WITH:
💊 MAOIs → hypertensive crisis (fatal)
☕ Excessive caffeine → heart rate stacking. Anxiety. Chest tightness. The college student combo.
🍷 Alcohol → Adderall masks alcohol's sedation. Drink more, feel less drunk, actual blood alcohol still rising. Blackout risk.
💊 Other stimulants → cardiac strain
💊 SSRIs → serotonin syndrome risk (low but present)

🔁 DEPENDENCY/TOLERANCE:
Tolerance builds. The dose that made them superhuman in month 1 is baseline by month 6. They need more to get the same effect. The doctor may or may not increase. If not: the black market. Or: the "drug holiday" where they don't take it on weekends and spend weekends in bed. The productivity on Adderall vs the person without Adderall become two different people. That gap widens with time.

📊 BSM-5 INTERACTIONS:
+ ADHD → the intended use. Works. The character can function. The question is whether they're "better" or just "faster."
+ Depression → sometimes prescribed off-label. Energizing. But the crash deepens the depression daily. Roller coaster.
+ Anxiety → makes it worse. Period. If this character has anxiety and is on Adderall, the anxiety is louder.
+ Substance Use → Adderall IS a substance of abuse. Schedule II. Cross-tolerance with cocaine and meth. The prescription pipeline.
+ Bipolar → stimulants can trigger mania. If this character is bipolar and on Adderall, someone is either very careful or very careless.

‼️ A CHARACTER IN THIS SCENE TAKES AMBIEN.
Ambien is the sleep drug that makes you do things. Driving, cooking, texting, having sex, having conversations — all with no memory of any of it. If this character takes Ambien and doesn't go directly to bed, they are entering a fugue state with their phone unlocked and their keys in reach. The amnesia gap between taking the pill and waking up is where the stories live.

✅ ON IT (just taken / active):
WENT TO BED: Asleep within 15-30 minutes. Deep, heavy, medicated sleep. Hard to wake. May sleep through alarms, noises, someone trying to rouse them. Morning grogginess.
STAYED UP: The Ambien twilight. Conscious but not forming memories. Disinhibited. Saying things, doing things, texting things they won't remember. Coordination impaired. Judgment gone. Appears awake. Is not meaningfully awake. This is where the stories come from.

❌ OFF IT (missed dose / discontinuation):
🟡 One night without: Rebound insomnia. Worse than the original insomnia. The brain forgot how to fall asleep without help.
🟠 Several nights: Can't sleep. At all. The insomnia is back and it brought reinforcements. Anxiety about sleep itself.
🔴 Long-term user stopping: Weeks of disrupted sleep. Anxiety. Irritability. Vivid dreams when sleep finally comes. The rebound can take a month to normalize.

⚠️ SIDE EFFECTS (the ones that show up in your writing):
Amnesia (the big one — no memory of what happened between pill and sleep) 🕳️ | complex sleep behaviors (driving, eating, texting, sex — while asleep) 🌙 | morning grogginess 😴 | dizziness 🫠 | hallucinations (if they fight the sleep) 👁️ | next-day impairment 🌫️ | sleepwalking 🚶 | bizarre behavior if awake on it 🤪 | emotional/disinhibited state

💀 DO NOT COMBINE WITH:
🍷 Alcohol → amplified amnesia, respiratory depression, the combination that creates "I have no idea what I did last night" on a Tuesday
💊 Benzos → compounded sedation. Redundant and dangerous.
💊 Opioids → respiratory depression
🍷 Any CNS depressant → stacking sedation

🔁 THE DEPENDENCY:
Ambien is prescribed for 2-4 weeks. People take it for years. The sleep without it doesn't come back easily. After a month of Ambien, the brain's natural sleep mechanism has atrophied. Stopping means relearning how to fall asleep, and during that relearning period, the insomnia is worse than ever. That's the trap. The drug that fixes sleep breaks sleep.

+ Anxiety → the 3AM anxiety spiral stops because you're unconscious. But the amnesia gap can create NEW anxiety. "What did I do?"
+ Substance Use → cross-dependency potential. The person who already has an addictive brain on a drug that creates physical dependency.

💉 BSM-5 PACKAGE INSERT — PREDNISONE (corticosteroid)
Read entire insert before writing character.

📋 DRUG CLASS: Corticosteroid (synthetic cortisol)
⏱️ TIMING: Onset 1-2 hrs → Duration: dose-dependent. Courses range from 5-day bursts to months/years of maintenance.
📦 PRESCRIBED FOR: Autoimmune conditions (lupus, RA, Crohn's, MS flares), severe asthma, allergic reactions, inflammation, organ transplant rejection prevention
⚠️ NOTE: Prednisone changes who you are. Not slowly. Not subtly. A character on a prednisone course is a different person than the character off it. The behavioral side effects are so dramatic they rival psychiatric conditions.

‼️ A CHARACTER IN THIS SCENE IS ON PREDNISONE.
Prednisone changes who a person is. Not slowly. Not subtly. A character on a prednisone course is a different person — mood swings from euphoria to rage to weeping, insatiable appetite, insomnia, physical changes (moon face, weight redistribution, skin thinning). A character on prednisone who isn't exhibiting prednisone effects is being written incorrectly. This drug is LOUD.

✅ ON IT (active course):
LOW DOSE / SHORT BURST: Energy surge. Euphoria even. Appetite skyrocketing. Can't sleep. Irritable but functional. Feeling "wired." Productive but snappy.
HIGH DOSE / LONG TERM: Moon face (the cheeks round out, the face changes shape). Weight gain concentrated in the trunk. Buffalo hump (fat deposits at the back of the neck). Skin thinning, bruising easily. Mood swings — euphoria to rage to crying in the same day. Insomnia (severe). Appetite (ravenous, constant, urgent). Muscle weakness. Acne. Facial hair growth. Bones weakening. Blood sugar spiking. The body is running on synthetic cortisol and it is NOT subtle.

❌ OFF IT / TAPERING:
🟡 Tapering (reducing dose): Fatigue. Joint pain returning. Mood dipping. The condition it was treating starts to resurface.
🟠 Tapered too fast: Adrenal crisis risk. The body's adrenal glands shut down during prednisone use (why make cortisol when the pill does it?). Stop too fast and the body has no cortisol at all. Nausea. Weakness. Dizziness. Potentially fatal.
🔴 Abrupt stop (long-term use): Medical emergency. Adrenal insufficiency. Vomiting. Shock. This drug MUST be tapered. The body needs time to restart cortisol production.

⚠️ SIDE EFFECTS (the ones that show up in your writing):
Moon face 🌝 | weight gain (central) 📈 | INSOMNIA (severe) 😵 | mood swings (euphoria/rage/weeping) 🎭 | insatiable appetite 🍽️ | irritability/rage ("roid rage" — real) 😤 | skin thinning/bruising easily 🩹 | acne 😖 | muscle weakness 💪📉 | buffalo hump | sweating 💦 | anxiety 😰 | elevated blood sugar 🩺 | bone density loss (long-term) 🦴 | immunosuppression — they catch everything

💀 DO NOT COMBINE WITH:
💊 NSAIDs → increased GI bleeding risk
💊 Blood thinners → bleeding risk
⚠️ Vaccines (live) → immunosuppressed, live vaccines are dangerous
💊 Diabetes meds → prednisone raises blood sugar, may need insulin adjustment
🦴 Long-term use without calcium/vitamin D → osteoporosis accelerates

🔁 THE TAPER:
You can't just stop. Reduce by small increments over weeks. The slower the taper, the safer. Every step down, the body is tested: can the adrenal glands wake up? The taper is its own experience — feeling worse at every step, wondering if the condition is coming back or if this is just withdrawal.

📊 BSM-5 INTERACTIONS:
+ Depression → prednisone can CAUSE depression. Or euphoria. The mood effects are unpredictable.
+ Bipolar → prednisone can trigger manic episodes. If this character is bipolar and needs prednisone, the psychiatrist and the prescribing doctor need to be talking. Are they?
+ Anxiety → the insomnia + irritability + wired feeling mimics anxiety disorder. Or worsens existing one.
+ BDD → moon face, weight redistribution, acne. The body changes. For someone with body image issues, prednisone is a nightmare.
+ Eating disorders → appetite becomes uncontrollable. The hunger is hormonal, not psychological. For someone with anorexia, this is a crisis. For someone with binge eating, this is a trigger.

💉 BSM-5 PACKAGE INSERT — INSULIN
Read entire insert before writing character.

📋 DRUG CLASS: Hormone (pancreatic replacement)
⏱️ TIMING: Rapid-acting: onset 15 min, duration 3-5 hrs | Long-acting: onset 1-2 hrs, duration 24 hrs
📦 PRESCRIBED FOR: Type 1 diabetes (mandatory — they produce zero insulin), Type 2 diabetes (when oral meds fail)
⚠️ NOTE: This is not optional medication. For Type 1 diabetics, no insulin = death. Days. Not weeks. Days. This is the most life-or-death medication on this list.

‼️ A CHARACTER IN THIS SCENE IS INSULIN-DEPENDENT.
For Type 1 diabetics, no insulin means death within days. This is the most life-or-death medication on this list. Insulin management is constant math: carbs consumed vs insulin dosed vs activity level vs stress vs illness vs time of day. Every meal is a calculation. Every unexpected event shifts the equation. There are no days off from diabetes. The management never stops.

✅ ON IT / WELL-MANAGED:
Blood sugar in range. Functional. Feels normal. But "normal" is maintained by constant effort: checking blood sugar (finger sticks or CGM — continuous glucose monitor), counting carbs, dosing insulin, timing meals. The CGM might beep. The insulin pump might need adjusting. There's always a device, a needle, a pen, a calculation. Well-managed diabetes is invisible to everyone except the person managing it.

❌ LOW BLOOD SUGAR (HYPOGLYCEMIA) — TOO MUCH INSULIN:
🟡 Mild (60-70 mg/dL): Shaky. Sweaty. Dizzy. Hungry suddenly and urgently. Confused. Irritable. Heart pounding. Need sugar NOW. Juice box. Glucose tabs. Anything fast.
🟠 Moderate (40-60): Can't think. Slurred speech. Vision blurry. Uncoordinated. Looks drunk. May not be able to help themselves. Someone else needs to give them sugar.
🔴 Severe (<40): Seizure. Loss of consciousness. Requires glucagon injection. Can be fatal. This is the emergency that lives in every insulin-dependent person's peripheral vision.

❌ HIGH BLOOD SUGAR (HYPERGLYCEMIA) — NOT ENOUGH INSULIN:
🟡 Mild: Thirsty. Peeing a lot. Tired. Blurry vision. Headache. Slower.
🟠 Prolonged high: Nausea. Confusion. Fruity breath (ketones). Muscle weakness.
🔴 DKA (Diabetic Ketoacidosis — Type 1): Medical emergency. The body is poisoning itself. Vomiting. Abdominal pain. Rapid breathing. Fruity breath. Confusion → coma → death. Hours, not days. Caused by missed insulin, pump failure, illness.

⚠️ LIFE DETAILS THAT SHOW UP IN WRITING:
Finger prick blood tests (or CGM on arm/stomach) 🩸 | insulin pen/syringe/pump 💉 | carb counting at every meal 🔢 | carrying fast-acting sugar everywhere 🧃 | the CGM alarm (beeps at high or low — during meetings, during sex, at 3AM) 📱 | injection sites (stomach, thigh, arm — rotation matters, lumps form) | the sharps container | the pharmacy relationship | the COST — insulin is expensive in the US. Rationing is real. People die from rationing.

💀 DANGEROUS SITUATIONS:
🏃 Exercise → drops blood sugar. Must eat beforehand or reduce insulin. A spontaneous run can become an emergency.
🍺 Alcohol → liver prioritizes metabolizing alcohol over releasing glucose. Blood sugar drops. Drunk + low blood sugar look identical. Which one is it?
🤒 Illness → blood sugar spikes. Insulin needs increase. Sick day protocol. Can't just "rest and recover" like everyone else.
🛫 Travel → time zones mess up dosing schedules. Temperature affects insulin (can't get too hot or cold). Always carry in hand luggage.

🔁 THE EXHAUSTION:
Diabetes burnout is real and documented. The relentless management. The constant math. The never-off-ness of it. Some people stop checking. Stop counting. Stop caring for periods. That's not laziness. That's a human being exhausted by a disease that requires them to manually run a system their body should automate. Write the burnout.

+ Depression → diabetes doubles the depression rate. The management burden + the chronic illness + the dietary restrictions + the cost + the social aspects = exhaustion → depression.
+ Eating disorders → insulin manipulation is its own eating disorder ("diabulimia"). Skip insulin to lose weight. Blood sugar runs high. Lose weight rapidly. Also: DKA. Also: organ damage. Also: death.

⏱️ TIMING: Infusion day → side effects peak 2-5 days later → cycle repeats every 2-4 weeks
📦 PRESCRIBED FOR: Cancer. The drug that poisons everything and hopes the cancer dies first.
⚠️ NOTE: Chemo is not one drug. It's dozens, in different combinations, for different cancers. The specifics change. The experience has common threads. Write the threads.

‼️ A CHARACTER IN THIS SCENE IS UNDERGOING CHEMOTHERAPY.
Chemo restructures a character's entire life around a cycle. Infusion day. The bad days after. The recovery window. Then the next infusion. Everything — work, relationships, plans, energy — orbits this calendar. The character knows exactly where they are in the cycle at all times. Each cycle stacks on the last. The cumulative toll deepens every round.

✅ ON TREATMENT (active cycle):
INFUSION DAY: Sitting in a chair for hours. IV in the port or arm. Cold cap maybe (to try to save the hair). Other patients in the room at various stages. The anti-nausea meds they give BEFORE the chemo — because the body knows what's coming. Sometimes fine during infusion. The storm hits later.

Can't eat but should eat. Bone-deep ache if on growth factor injections. Immune system cratered — a cold could hospitalize them.
RECOVERY WINDOW (days 7-14): Energy slowly returning. Starting to feel human. Eating again. Knowing the next infusion is coming. The countdown to doing it all over again.

❌ BETWEEN CYCLES / CUMULATIVE EFFECTS:
Each cycle stacks. Cycle 1 is manageable. Cycle 4 is harder. Cycle 6 is surviving. The cumulative fatigue deepens. The body has less to recover with each time. "Chemo brain" — cognitive fog, word-finding difficulty, memory problems — can last months to years after treatment ends.

⚠️ EFFECTS THAT SHOW UP IN WRITING:

🤒 Fever → neutropenic fever is a medical emergency. Temperature over 100.4 on chemo = ER immediately. The immune system can't fight infection.
🩸 Bleeding/bruising → platelets may be low. A cut that won't stop. A bruise from nothing.
🤝 Sick people → someone with a cold is a genuine threat. The character avoids crowds, planes, children in daycare, hospitals ironically.
💊 Drug interactions → the oncologist manages everything. Random supplements, OTC drugs, herbal remedies can all interfere.

🔁 THE CALENDAR:
Chemo patients count days. "I'm on day 3 of cycle 4." "My next infusion is Thursday." "I have 2 cycles left." The treatment has a structure and the patient knows exactly where they are in it at all times. The countdown to the end of treatment is hope and math combined.

⚠️ NOTE: HRT covers very different populations. A trans woman on estrogen, a trans man on testosterone, and a menopausal woman on HRT have different drugs, different goals, different experiences. The common thread: hormones change everything slowly.

‼️ A CHARACTER IN THIS SCENE IS ON HRT.
Hormones are not a switch. They're a season change — slow, cumulative, irreversible in some ways and reversible in others. A character on HRT is in a body that is actively changing. How far along they are determines what's visible, what's still coming, and what the emotional landscape looks like. The waiting for changes IS the daily experience.

✅ ON IT (GENDER-AFFIRMING — ESTROGEN):
Months 1-3: Breast buds (tender, sore). Skin softening. Reduced libido. Emotional range expanding — crying more easily, feelings hitting harder. Less spontaneous erections. Body odor changing.
Months 3-12: Breast development continuing. Fat redistribution starting (hips, thighs, face). Muscle mass decreasing. Skin softer. Body hair thinning. Facial hair unchanged (requires electrolysis/laser separately).
Year 1+: Body feminization continuing slowly. Breast growth can take 2-5 years. Infertility likely. Testicular atrophy. Emotional baseline shifted — different from pre-HRT in ways that are hard to articulate.

✅ ON IT (GENDER-AFFIRMING — TESTOSTERONE):
Months 1-3: Voice starting to crack/deepen. Increased libido (significantly). Bottom growth (clitoral enlargement). Oilier skin. Acne. Body odor changing (stronger). Emotional shift — some describe it as "feeling less" or "feeling differently."
Months 3-12: Voice deepening (permanent). Facial hair starting (patchy, slow). Fat redistribution (face angularity, waist). Muscle mass increasing. Periods stopping (usually by 6 months).
Year 1+: Full voice change. Facial hair continuing to develop (can take years). Male-pattern hair loss possible. Body hair increasing. Permanent changes: voice, facial hair, bottom growth.

✅ ON IT (MENOPAUSAL HRT):
Hot flashes reduced or eliminated. Sleep improved. Mood stabilized. Vaginal dryness addressed. Bone density maintained. Cognitive clarity improved. The thing that was making menopause miserable — managed. Quality of life restoration.

❌ OFF IT / INTERRUPTED:
🟡 Missed doses (gender-affirming): Mood instability. Hot flashes (estrogen). Energy dip (testosterone). The body notices quickly.
🟠 Forced discontinuation: Emotional crisis. Dysphoria returning or intensifying. Body changes stalling or reversing (some, not all). For trans people, losing access to HRT is not a minor medical inconvenience — it's an identity crisis with physical symptoms.
🟠 Menopause HRT stopped: Hot flashes return. Sleep disruption returns. Symptoms return. Often immediately.

⚠️ EFFECTS THAT SHOW UP IN WRITING:
ESTROGEN: Emotional sensitivity 😢 | breast tenderness | softer skin | reduced muscle | changed libido | hot flashes (if dose is off) | mood swings during adjustment | injection day routine 💉

💀 MEDICAL CONSIDERATIONS:
💊 Estrogen + smoking → significant blood clot risk. If this character smokes and takes estrogen, this is a real danger.
🩸 Testosterone → polycythemia (blood thickening). Needs regular blood work. Can cause stroke if unmonitored.
💊 Anti-androgens (spironolactone) → potassium levels, blood pressure, frequent urination
⚠️ All HRT → requires regular blood work. Hormone levels checked. Liver function. Blood counts. The medical maintenance is ongoing.

🔁 THE WAITING:
Gender-affirming HRT is measured in "when will I see changes." The timeline is agonizingly slow. Changes happen over months and years, not days. The character checks the mirror constantly. Compares photos. Measures. Notices things nobody else notices yet. The waiting is the experience. The body is catching up to the identity and it takes its goddamn time.

📊 BSM-5 INTERACTIONS:
+ Gender dysphoria → HRT is the treatment. The relationship between the medication and the condition is direct. Progress reduces dysphoria. Stalls or setbacks amplify it.

💉 BSM-5 PACKAGE INSERT — BIRTH CONTROL (hormonal contraceptives)
Read entire insert before writing character.

📋 DRUG CLASS: Hormonal contraceptive (estrogen + progestin OR progestin-only)
📦 PRESCRIBED FOR: Preventing pregnancy. Also: period regulation, endometriosis, PCOS, acne, PMDD, fibroids, ovarian cysts
⚠️ NOTE: "On birth control" is not enough information. WHICH birth control? WHY? Since when? The method, the reason, and the side effect profile are three different character details and they all matter.

‼️ A CHARACTER IN THIS SCENE IS ON BIRTH CONTROL.
First question: what kind. Second question: why. Not everyone on birth control is preventing pregnancy. The teenager put on it for crippling periods. The woman managing endometriosis. The person with PCOS who needs it to prevent cysts. The person who IS using it for pregnancy prevention. The reason shapes the relationship with the medication — "I take this so I don't get pregnant" is a different emotional register than "I take this so I can function during my period."

📋 THE TYPES — THESE ARE DIFFERENT DRUGS WITH DIFFERENT EXPERIENCES:

💊 COMBINED PILL (estrogen + progestin):
Daily pill. Same time every day. The alarm on the phone. The pack with the days of the week. 21 active + 7 placebo (withdrawal bleed) or continuous (skip the placebos, skip the period). Miss a day? Window depends on the pill — some give 12 hrs, some 24. Miss two? That's a problem. Brands matter — low estrogen vs standard vs high; different progestins have different side effect profiles. Lo Loestrin is different from Ortho Tri-Cyclen is different from Yaz. The trial-and-error of finding "the right one" can take years.

💉 DEPO-PROVERA (injection):
Shot every 3 months. Progestin only. Get it at the doctor's office. No daily maintenance. Periods often stop completely. BUT: weight gain (5-10 lbs average, sometimes more), bone density loss with long-term use (2+ years), delayed return to fertility (can take 6-18 months after stopping). The shot you can't un-take — if the side effects are bad, you're stuck for 3 months.

💪 NEXPLANON (arm implant):
Matchstick-sized rod inserted in the upper arm. Progestin only. Lasts 3 years. Set it and forget it. Periods may stop, become irregular, or become unpredictable spotting for months. The rod is palpable under the skin — the character can feel it, a partner might feel it. Insertion/removal is a minor procedure. Most effective method available (99.95%).

🔄 NUVARING (vaginal ring):
Flexible ring inserted vaginally. Worn 3 weeks, removed 1 week. Combined hormones absorbed through vaginal wall. The character inserts and removes it herself. Can be felt during sex (by either partner). Must be refrigerated before use. Falls out sometimes. The "did the ring come out during sex?" anxiety.

🩹 THE PATCH (Xulane):
Stick it on — buttock, abdomen, arm, back. Change weekly. Visible if not hidden by clothing. Can peel. Can fall off in the shower. Delivers hormones through skin. Less effective in women over 198 lbs (this is on the label and rarely discussed).

⚒ IUD — HORMONAL (Mirena, Kyleena, Liletta, Skyla):
T-shaped device inserted into the uterus. The insertion is a whole experience — cramping, sometimes severe, sometimes described as "the worst pain I've ever felt," sometimes just uncomfortable. Lasts 3-8 years depending on brand. Local hormone release. Periods usually lighten or stop. Strings hang from the cervix — checking strings monthly, partners sometimes feel them. Expulsion risk (it can come out). Perforation risk (rare but it can embed in the uterine wall).

⚒ IUD — COPPER (Paragard):
Non-hormonal. The only non-hormonal long-acting option. Copper is toxic to sperm. Lasts up to 10 years. NO hormonal side effects. BUT: heavier periods. Worse cramps. Sometimes significantly worse. The character who chose copper chose it because she wanted NO hormones — that's a character detail about her relationship with synthetic hormones.

⚠️ WHY SHE'S ON IT — THE REASON MATTERS:

🛡️ PREGNANCY PREVENTION: The obvious one. But even here — is it her choice? Mutual decision? Partner pressure? Is she the only one managing contraception? Is there resentment about that?

🩸 PERIOD MANAGEMENT: Periods so heavy she's anemic. Cramps so bad she misses work. Irregular cycles that make life unpredictable. Birth control as medical management, not contraception. She might not even be sexually active.

🧬 PCOS: Polycystic ovarian syndrome. Birth control regulates the hormonal chaos. Without it: irregular periods, cysts, acne, excess hair growth, fertility concerns. The pill is managing a chronic condition.

🔥 ENDOMETRIOSIS: Tissue growing where it shouldn't. Pain during periods, pain during sex, pain at random. Birth control suppresses growth. Often continuous (no placebo week) to prevent the hormonal cycling that feeds endo.

😤 PMDD: Premenstrual dysphoric disorder. Not PMS. PMDD is debilitating — depression, rage, anxiety, suicidal ideation in the luteal phase. Certain pills (Yaz specifically) are FDA-approved for PMDD. The birth control is a psychiatric medication for her.

❌ SIDE EFFECTS (these ARE the daily experience):
Mood changes — depression, anxiety, emotional flattening, irritability 😶 | reduced libido (the contraceptive that kills desire — ironic and common) 📉 | weight gain/bloating | breast tenderness | headaches/migraines (estrogen-containing can worsen migraines with aura — stroke risk) 🤕 | nausea 🤢 | breakthrough bleeding/spotting | blood clot risk (estrogen-containing — DVT, PE, stroke) 🩸 | acne (some pills clear it, some cause it) | hair changes | the libido thing bears repeating: many people on hormonal BC have significantly reduced desire and NEVER connect it to the pill because they started it at 16 and don't know what their baseline libido actually is

⚠️ RISK FACTORS — WHO SHOULDN'T BE ON WHAT:
🚬 Smoking + estrogen-containing BC + over 35 = blood clots, stroke, heart attack. Real risk. Doctors should refuse to prescribe combined pills to smokers over 35.
🧠 Migraines with aura + estrogen = stroke risk. Progestin-only methods only.
🩸 History of blood clots = no estrogen. Period.
📏 Weight over 198 lbs = patch less effective. Weight over 155 lbs = Plan B less effective.
🧬 Family history of clots, breast cancer, liver disease = all affect which methods are safe.
🤰 Breastfeeding = no estrogen (affects milk supply). Progestin-only ok.

❌ STOPPED / COMING OFF:
🟡 Missed pills: Breakthrough bleeding. Pregnancy risk. The anxiety spiral of "when exactly did I miss it, did we have sex, do I need Plan B."
🟠 Stopped entirely: Hormonal readjustment over weeks-months. Period returns (timing unpredictable). Skin may break out. Mood shifts — either direction. Libido may surge back. Some women describe it as meeting themselves for the first time. Others describe it as hormonal chaos. Both are accurate.
🟠 IUD removal: Cramping. Return to baseline cycles quickly (hormonal) or immediately (copper).
🟠 Post-Depo: Delayed fertility return. Up to 18 months. The character who stopped Depo to get pregnant and now can't — that's a specific frustration.

💀 INTERACTIONS:
💊 Modafinil → reduces pill effectiveness (enzyme induction)
💊 Some antibiotics (rifampin specifically, NOT most antibiotics despite the myth) → reduces effectiveness
🌿 St. John's Wort → reduces effectiveness
💊 Some anticonvulsants → reduce effectiveness (relevant if character has epilepsy)
🍷 Vomiting within 2 hrs of taking the pill → may not have absorbed. Same as a missed dose.

🔁 THE INVISIBLE LABOR:
The daily alarm. The pharmacy refill. The insurance negotiation. The annual exam to renew the prescription. The side effect management that nobody asks about. The trial and error of formulations. The assumption that contraception is her responsibility. The partner who has never had to think about any of this. Write the labor. Write the asymmetry.

📊 BSM-5 INTERACTIONS:
+ Depression → hormonal BC can cause or worsen depression. Research finally backs what women have said for decades. Character started the pill at 16, started being depressed at 17 — that's pharmacology, not coincidence.
+ PMDD → some pills treat it (Yaz). Others worsen it. The hormonal roulette.
+ Anxiety → hormonal changes modulate anxiety. Some formulations help. Some amplify. Trial and error is the experience.
+ Eating disorders → weight gain side effect + body conflict = crisis. Amenorrhea from the eating disorder masked by the pill's artificial bleed. "My period's regular" — is it? Or is the pill faking one?

+ Libido/relationship → desire reduced by the pill creates relationship tension nobody names. "I'm just not in the mood" for months/years. Is it her? The relationship? Or the 0.035mg of ethinyl estradiol?

💉 BSM-5 PACKAGE INSERT — INHALER (albuterol / maintenance steroids)
Read entire insert before writing character.

📋 DRUG CLASS: Rescue bronchodilator (albuterol) + maintenance corticosteroid (fluticasone, budesonide, etc.)
⏱️ TIMING: Rescue: onset 5-15 min, duration 4-6 hrs | Maintenance: daily, prevents attacks over time
📦 PRESCRIBED FOR: Asthma. Exercise-induced bronchoconstriction. COPD.
⚠️ NOTE: Two inhalers, two jobs. The rescue (usually blue) opens the airways NOW during an attack. The maintenance (usually brown/orange/purple) prevents attacks over time. The character who only has the rescue inhaler isn't managing their asthma — they're just surviving each attack. The one who takes the maintenance daily and still carries the rescue is managing it properly and still scared.

‼️ A CHARACTER IN THIS SCENE HAS ASTHMA AND CARRIES AN INHALER.
Asthma is a body that can't be trusted to breathe. The airways can constrict from exercise, cold air, dust, mold, stress, smoke, or nothing at all. The rescue inhaler is the thing between this character and suffocation. They know where it is at all times — the bag, the pocket, the nightstand. The moment of "where is it" during an attack is terror.

✅ RESCUE INHALER (during attack):
Can't breathe. Chest tight like a band. Wheezing — the whistling on exhale that everyone in the room can hear. Coughing. Sitting upright, leaning forward, shoulders up, neck muscles straining — the body recruiting every accessory muscle to force air in. Shake the inhaler. Breathe out. Inhale the puff. Hold 10 seconds. Wait. Another puff if needed. The albuterol relaxes the airway muscles. Air comes back. Heart racing (albuterol is a stimulant). Hands shaky. Jittery. Wired. The relief is physical and emotional simultaneously.

✅ MAINTENANCE INHALER (daily):
Morning. Evening. Every day. Inhale the steroid. Rinse mouth after (thrush risk — yeast infection in the mouth from steroid residue). No immediate effect. No rescue. Just slow, daily prevention. The boring one. The one people stop taking because "I feel fine" and then can't figure out why the attacks came back. Adherence is the whole game.

❌ WITHOUT IT:
🟡 Mild attack, no rescue: Sitting still. Controlled breathing. Trying to relax the airways manually. Caffeine (mild bronchodilator). Riding it out. This works for mild attacks. Doesn't work for bad ones.
🟠 Moderate attack, no rescue: Can't talk in full sentences. Only a few words per breath. Visible distress. Needs help. Needs the inhaler or needs 911.
🔴 Severe attack, no rescue: Silent chest (the wheezing STOPS because no air is moving). Blue lips. Altered consciousness. Medical emergency. People die from asthma attacks. Not often, but the possibility lives in every asthmatic's peripheral vision.

⚠️ DETAILS THAT SHOW UP IN WRITING:
The shake-exhale-inhale-hold ritual 💨 | jitteriness after rescue use (stimulant effect) 🫨 | the wheezing sound | the posture during an attack (upright, leaning forward, accessory muscles) | coughing as a symptom | knowing your triggers (cold, exercise, allergens, smoke, stress) | pre-medicating before exercise | the spacer (tube some people use for better delivery) | the midnight attack — waking up can't breathe | steroid voice (hoarse from maintenance inhaler) | the rescue inhaler's location — always known

💀 MEDICAL INTERACTIONS:
⚠️ Beta-blockers (propranolol) + asthma = DANGEROUS. Beta-blockers can trigger bronchospasm. If this character has anxiety and asthma, propranolol could send them to the ER.
🚬 Smoking + asthma = accelerated lung damage. Also: secondhand smoke as a trigger.
💊 NSAIDs (aspirin, ibuprofen) can trigger attacks in some asthmatics (aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease).
😤 Stress → asthma attacks. The psychosomatic component is real. The emotional trigger is a physical trigger.

🔁 THE CARRYING:
The inhaler is always in the bag. Check before leaving. Check at the restaurant. Check at the gym. The expired one that needs replacing. The backup in the car. The one at the office. The one at the boyfriend's house. The distribution of rescue inhalers across the character's life is a map of where they spend time and where they feel safe.

📊 BSM-5 INTERACTIONS:
+ Anxiety → health anxiety that's justified. Every tight breath is: "Is this an attack or anxiety?" The overlap between panic attack and asthma attack — same symptoms, different cause, different treatment. Getting it wrong matters.
+ Panic disorder → panic attacks cause hyperventilation and chest tightness. Asthma attacks cause chest tightness and difficulty breathing. The character may use the rescue inhaler during a panic attack (it won't help but the ritual calms them) or may assume an asthma attack is "just panic" and not treat it (dangerous).
+ PTSD → previous severe attacks can be traumatic. ICU stays. Intubation. The fear of it happening again IS hypervigilance but it's also medically rational.
+ Depression → chronic illness fatigue. The daily maintenance that never ends. The limitation on activity. The "I can't do that" list.
+ Exercise avoidance → exercise-induced asthma limits activity. The character who should exercise for their mental health but literally can't breathe when they do.
