35.content:
💉 BSM-5 PACKAGE INSERT — EPIPEN (epinephrine auto-injector)
Read entire insert before writing character.

📋 DRUG CLASS: Epinephrine (adrenaline) auto-injector
⏱️ TIMING: Onset: SECONDS → Duration: 15-20 minutes. That's it. 15-20 minutes. It's a bridge, not a cure.
📦 PRESCRIBED FOR: Anaphylaxis — severe allergic reaction. Bee stings. Peanuts. Shellfish. Tree nuts. Medication allergies. Latex. The character knows their trigger and lives around it.
⚠️ NOTE: An EpiPen is a loaded gun that fires adrenaline. It exists because without it, this character can die from a food, a sting, or a touch. That reality shapes every meal, every restaurant, every new environment, every kiss from someone who ate the wrong thing.

‼️ A CHARACTER IN THIS SCENE CARRIES AN EPIPEN.
This character's body has a kill switch triggered by something most people encounter casually — a food, a sting, a material. They have mapped their entire life around avoiding it. The EpiPen is the backup plan for when avoidance fails. They carry two, they check the expiration, they know which pocket it's in without looking. This isn't anxiety. This is survival infrastructure.

✅ THE ALLERGEN — WHAT'S THE TRIGGER?
🥜 PEANUTS/TREE NUTS: The most common severe food allergy. Traces in cooking oil, cross-contamination, "may contain" labels. The character reads every label. Asks at every restaurant. Can't eat anything they didn't vet. Airborne particles can trigger reactions in severe cases. Kissing someone who ate peanuts can trigger it. The allergen is social as much as physical.
🦐 SHELLFISH: Restaurants are minefields. Cross-contamination in shared fryers. The steam from cooking shellfish can trigger. Iodine allergy overlap is a myth but the character may believe it.
🐝 INSECT STINGS: Outdoor activities carry risk. The buzzing is the warning. The character who flinches at every bee isn't anxious — they're reasonable. Gardening, picnics, hikes — all calculated risks.
💊 MEDICATION: Penicillin, sulfa drugs, NSAIDs, contrast dye. The medical bracelet. The allergy list that must be communicated at every appointment, every ER visit. "I'M ALLERGIC TO—" when they can't speak is why the bracelet exists.
🧤 LATEX: Gloves. Condoms. Balloons. Band-aids. Medical settings are full of latex. The character who carries non-latex alternatives. The sexual partner who has to use specific condoms.

🚨 ANAPHYLAXIS — THE EVENT:
STAGE 1 (minutes): Itching. Hives spreading. Throat feels "thick." Lips/tongue tingling or swelling. Stomach cramping. Anxiety — the "something is wrong" recognition.
STAGE 2 (escalating): Throat closing. Voice changes — hoarse, tight. Difficulty breathing. Wheezing. Blood pressure dropping. Dizzy. Nauseous. Skin flushing or going pale.
STAGE 3 (emergency): Can't breathe. Can't talk. Blood pressure crashed. Vomiting. Loss of consciousness. MINUTES TO DEATH.

💉 THE EPIPEN:
Blue cap off. Orange end against outer thigh. Push HARD — through clothes if necessary. CLICK. Hold 10 seconds. Pull out. Adrenaline hits. Heart rate surges. Airways open. Blood pressure stabilizes. Shaking. Wired. Scared. The reaction SLOWS but doesn't stop — the EpiPen is buying time. Call 911 EVERY TIME. The reaction can return in 4-6 hours (biphasic reaction). Hospital observation required. One EpiPen might not be enough — that's why they carry two.

❌ WITHOUT IT:
No EpiPen + anaphylaxis = medical emergency with no bridge medication. Throat closing. Airway gone. This is the scenario that keeps this character and everyone who loves them awake at night. The forgotten bag. The expired pen. The day they didn't bring it because "I'll only be gone an hour." That's the nightmare.

⚠️ PRACTICAL DETAILS THAT SHOW UP IN WRITING:
The auto-injector in the bag (always) 💉 | carrying TWO (standard) | checking expiration dates | the thigh bruise after use 🩹 | the adrenaline aftermath (shaking, racing heart, anxiety for hours) ⚡ | reading every label 🏷️ | asking at every restaurant 🍽️ | medical alert bracelet/necklace ⚕️ | the cost ($300+ for a 2-pack, US) 💸 | temperature sensitivity (can't leave in hot car/cold car) 🌡️ | the EpiPen trainer (practice device with no needle) | teaching partners/friends/coworkers how to use it

💀 INTERACTIONS:
⚠️ Beta-blockers (propranolol) + anaphylaxis = the EpiPen may not work effectively. Beta-blockers oppose epinephrine. If this character has anxiety treated with propranolol AND carries an EpiPen, there's a genuine conflict between treating the anxiety and being able to survive an allergic reaction.
💊 ACE inhibitors → can worsen anaphylaxis
⚠️ The allergen itself — trace amounts. Cross-contamination. Shared cooking surfaces. Kissing someone who ate it hours ago. The character's vigilance is proportional to how invisible the trigger can be.

🔁 THE VIGILANCE:
Every new restaurant: "Do you have a nut-free menu?" Every party: "What's in this?" Every date: "I need to tell you something before we eat together." Every label, every ingredient list, every "may contain traces of." The vigilance is exhausting and necessary and never ends. The character who relaxes their guard is the character who ends up on the floor with a needle in their thigh.

📊 BSM-5 INTERACTIONS:
+ Anxiety → the hypervigilance is medically required. But it's still exhausting. The overlap between "appropriately cautious" and "anxious" is complete. Health anxiety that is 100% justified still feels like health anxiety.
+ Social anxiety → the explaining. Every meal. Every new person. "I can't eat that." "Can you check the kitchen?" The character who avoids social eating entirely rather than navigate the conversation.
+ PTSD → previous anaphylactic episodes are traumatic. The ER. The needle. The not-being-able-to-breathe. The helplessness. Subsequent exposures trigger trauma responses on top of allergic responses.
+ OCD → contamination checking that looks like OCD but is medically necessary. Where's the line between "checking the label three times" as OCD and "checking the label three times" as staying alive?
+ Eating disorders → food restriction with medical justification layered over psychological restriction. Avoidance of entire food groups because of allergy + avoidance of food because of the disorder. Which limits are medical and which are the illness? Nearly impossible to untangle from outside.
